notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware, ROS 2, Gazebo or upstream-simulator run was made. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's helper is RosDriver/family ros, but the confirmed entry rl_racing.gazebo_env:GazeboEnv (gazebo_env.py:11) is a Gymnasium environment registered as RacingBotEnv-v0 (start_learning.py:36-40); its primary interface is step/reset, not a ROS topic or service, so this package uses GymnasiumDriver and the bridge serves cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1. The repository also contains ROS nodes, but wrapping those would not preserve the environment-step interface. The fake backend is a pure Python analytic kinematic stand-in (not a recording): it copies the upstream action space (gazebo_env.py:25-27), observation scaling (105-110), crash test (112-119) and reward terms (121-145), and returns 60 beams, the declared observation size. The action_space_ref is rl_racing/rl_racing/gazebo_env.py:25-27, so the derived step bounds are upstream_code. The fake models no Gazebo physics, contacts, laser rays, odometry, sensor noise or rendering; its 60-beam profile is placeholder test data and was never compared with a Gazebo run. The e-stop is the runtime's software latch: no native stop exists and no hardware backend is declared. The upstream simulator was not run because it needs ROS 2 Humble, Gazebo, rclpy and gymnasium, and the clone is read-only and never imported by package code. The clone's URDF declares a front_laser link but contains no Gazebo LaserScan plugin, so the real /front_laser/scan publisher and beam configuration are not shown; a live run needs the operator's Gazebo setup. The fake has no physical timestep (fidelity.timestep_ms=0, no wall-clock pacing); one cap.world.step.v1 tick is one fake control transition. The implicit sim backend (gym.make of RacingBotEnv-v0) is not runnable from the package alone because the registration lives only in start_learning.main (start_learning.py:36-40). No returned array is reduced. Expected warnings: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the bridge only stores the pending seed and makes no native call) and four G8.NO_UNIT for the bridge-derived inputs (seed on reset, seed on seed, ticks and action.values). G4 reported no REF_VALUE or REF_BINARY warnings. Only catalogue classes are used, so there are no catalogue requests. driver.lock.json keeps reviewed_by null.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the GymnasiumDriver deviation, all 24 facts, action_space_ref, the fake and the stop text against gazebo_env.py, gazebo_connections.py, start_learning.py, the launch files and the td_robot model at the pin. The deviation is right (GazeboEnv is a gymnasium.Env whose ROS topics are internal transport), but the safe_state said the simulated world stops advancing although Gazebo is free-running and the upstream never pauses it or publishes a zero Twist; two gaps and an author note said the clone shows no laser publisher or beam configuration, while the included td_robot model SDF has the 60-sample 0.1 to 10 laser on /front_laser/scan and the diff-drive plugin (td_robot.sdf:340-366, 727-750); three facts said more than their lines (the Node base class is on another file, the [0, 1] range and the 0.2 threshold come from lines 20-23), and the spin and resetSim facts omitted that they wait without a deadline. The reviewer rewrote safe_state, those five facts and the two gaps, added four source facts and gaps for the unbounded spin and reset waits, the global rclpy.init, the 1000-step registration the fake does not apply, the odometry velocity the fake replaces by the command, the upstream's scaled-versus-unscaled safety penalty and the documented trainer launch that publishes /cmd_vel itself (driver.py); marked the fake's velocity as a placeholder for odometry (fake.py), said so in the reward case and labelled the two seed cases fake-only, because the upstream seed reaches no generator the world uses (test_driver.py); updated facts.md; and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate and collect.py --strict pass with the expected G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL and G8.NO_UNIT warnings and the digest unchanged; the author's notes on the missing laser plugin and on the latch stopping the world are superseded. For the human reviewer: Fake-only contract; no sim backend is declared, and gymnasium.make in the server finds no RacingBotEnv-v0 because only start_learning.main registers it. A live environment would need a prior global rclpy.init(), and its step and reset wait without deadlines for laser, odometry and /reset_simulation. The latch sends nothing: Gazebo keeps running with the last /cmd_vel Twist. The environment uses the generic root /cmd_vel, /odom and /front_laser/scan and nothing in it checks for a simulator, so in a ROS graph with a real base on /cmd_vel it would command that base; the documented start_training.launch.py runs a TD3 trainer that publishes /cmd_vel itself and must not run beside MHS.

MODEL REVIEW (grok-4.7, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Item 12 repair. GazeboEnv.step calls _set_action, which publishes geometry_msgs/Twist linear.x and angular.z on /cmd_vel (gazebo_env.py:44-47 and 95-103; gazebo_connections.py:36-39 and 47-51). td_robot.sdf:727-750 points libgazebo_ros_diff_drive at command_topic cmd_vel and does not say that only that plugin consumes it, so the class risk is R2, a mobile base. safe_state and facts.md say the latch publishes no zero Twist and does not stop a base on /cmd_vel. The reference was regenerated. python3 -m mhs.driver check --backend fake passed with the same stable digest sha256:d4bebc0e1334584b100d8a55afd649662a5bf17b363ce2396737fe26764018fe, and G9 passed. Evidence is contract_checked on the fake only. reviewed_by stays null.

MODEL REVIEW (gpt-6.1-sol, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Different-model review by Codex (gpt-6.1-sol) of the work of Grok (grok-4.7), unit p5-backlog-packages--bl04, round 1: Traced step through _set_action and publish_velocity to /cmd_vel. R2 is appropriate, and the revised description accurately states that the latch sends no zero velocity command. Strict collection passed. For the human reviewer: A physical consumer of /cmd_vel remains outside the demonstrated stop contract.
